Frequently asked questions | Kickstart Innovation top of page Login to my kickstart Kickstart FAQs Q: Does Kickstart invest in startups? At the moment there are no investment activities on our behalf, however Kickstart organizes curtain events including the annual Investor Summit that aims to bring participating startups together with investors. Q: Why would Switzerland be an attractive location for international startups? Switzerland is one of the countries with the best environment for entrepreneurial activities. The number of companies being founded in Switzerland has been growing for several years. The stable economic framework and market, the strong education sector, the world-class infrastructure and the high quality of life are just some of the positive aspects that make Switzerland attractive for startups. Furthermore, Switzerland is one of the most important financial centers worldwide and many leading international corporations as well as leading technical universities such as ETH Zurich are based in Switzerland. We have seen a growing appetite within the corporate sector to collaborate with startups, already surmounting to +340 fruitful collaborations. Q: Is Kickstart a non-profit organization (NPO)? No, Kickstart Innovation AG is a for-profit company. Q: Why is Kickstart focusing on later-stage startups? What does “later stage” mean in this context? Later-stage
Later-stage refers to mature startups, or so-called “scale-ups” that already have a technology and potential product in the market.

We see more eye-level collaboration happening between scale-ups and established companies and we thus increase the likelihood of successful collaborations such as PoCs, pilot projects or commercial partnerships.
Throughout the program, the founders receive free coworking-space in the innovation space Kraftwerk in the heart of Zurich.
Most of the startups from the earlier cohorts have built up or enhanced relationships in Switzerland.
So far, at least 30% of our international alumni startups have offices or staff in Switzerland.

To convene deep tech high-growth ventures together with multiple organisations such as companies, universities, foundations and cities to foster the Swiss ecosystem innovation and sustainable development.

Through collaboration

Through collaboration across verticals and industries as well as between startups and corporates, Kickstart Accelerator 2016 put Switzerland on the international map of startup and digital innovation hubs.
It offered foreign entrepreneurial talent fast-track access to the Swiss startup ecosystem and corporate partners, establishing long-term relationships across the globe.

2017 Kickstart Accelerator becomes an Impact Hub program, gaining access to a global network that connects more than 16,000 entrepreneurs, creatives and techies into a collaborative ecosystem across 100+ Impact Hubs.
Only 1 year after its launch, Kickstart Accelerator gathers the support of more than 60 partner organizations and launches 2 new verticals: Robotics & Intelligent Systems and Smart Cities.
2018 Kickstart Accelerator officially launches its 6th vertical - EdTech & Learning, and engages an ever increasing diversity of partners.

We introduced our first Investor Summit, bringing together over 100 investors (Business Angels, Family Offices, Venture Capital, Corporate Venture Capital, Funds of Funds), startups and partners to participate in the summit, profiling first-rate speakers and top pitches.
From 6 collaborations each year in 2016 and 2017, Kickstart Accelerator facilitates 35 collaborations in 2018 between startups and partners!
2019 Kickstart Accelerator becomes Kickstart Innovation - as an independent program with a stronger focus on commercial collaborations with late-stage startups .

30% of international startups stay in Switzerland after completing the Kickstart program, confirming Kickstart’s contribution to the enhancement of Switzerland as an attractive market for innovative startups.

2020 Despite the hybrid and online engagement formats, Kickstart reaches a new record in number of PoCs per edition since launch - 40, as well as a new record in people engaged through activities: 1’500. ​ Kickstart and Impact Hub Switzerland join forces to launch the Circular Economy cross-vertical in the Kickstart program, to support technological innovations for sustainable development.

ZURICH, 5th August 2020 - The new application phase for the 3rd Swiss Market Entry Bootcamp begins today and lasts until 1 September. This initiative of digitalswitzerland offers 50 startups a deep insight into the Swiss ecosystem. The program is run by Kickstart Innovation, one of the largest innovation platforms in Europe. "Switzerland is a global innovation leader, as the Global Innovation Index has confirmed in its ranking," explain Nicolas Bürer and Matthias Zwingli from digitalswitzerland. "50 startups are given the opportunity to meet with experts from leading corporations, public institutions, innovation programs, accelerators and incubators, not only to further develop their concepts, but also to boost a possible market entry in Switzerland".
